subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which salt is formed when hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide?
questions.explain: Hydrochloric acid produces chloride salts, so sodium chloride is formed.

questions.q: Which name correctly describes ethanoic acid?
questions.explain: Ethanoic acid only partially ionises in water, so it is a weak acid.

questions.q: A weak acid and a strong acid have the same pH. Which statement is true?
options: The strong acid is more concentrated
The weak acid is more concentrated
questions.explain: Because a weak acid only partially ionises, it needs a higher concentration to reach the same pH.

questions.q: Mendeleev sometimes placed elements out of strict mass order so that they:
options: Fitted with others having similar properties
questions.explain: He switched some elements so they lined up with others of similar chemical properties.

questions.q: A substance that does not move from the baseline in chromatography is most likely:
questions.explain: A spot that stays on the baseline is insoluble in that solvent and does not travel.

questions.q: Which metal will displace copper from copper sulfate solution?
questions.explain: Iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from copper sulfate solution.

questions.q: When silver nitrate is added to a solution containing iodide ions, the precipitate is:
questions.explain: Iodide ions form a yellow precipitate of silver iodide.

questions.q: Why does oiling or greasing iron tools help prevent rusting?
options: It makes the iron more reactive
It keeps out water and oxygen
questions.explain: A barrier of oil keeps water and oxygen away from the iron surface.

questions.q: A pure substance, unlike a mixture, will:
options: Melt and boil at specific sharp temperatures
Melt over a range of temperatures
questions.explain: A pure substance has a sharp, specific melting and boiling point, whereas mixtures melt and boil over a range.

questions.q: Calcium ions give which colour in a flame test?
questions.explain: Calcium ions produce an orange-red flame.

questions.q: When making a soluble salt from an insoluble base and acid, why is excess base added?
options: To ensure all the acid is neutralised
questions.explain: Excess insoluble base guarantees all the acid reacts; the leftover solid is then filtered off.

questions.q: Why are the Group 0 noble gases unreactive?
options: They have a full outer shell of electrons
questions.explain: Noble gases have full (stable) outer electron shells, so they rarely react.

questions.q: What colour does universal indicator turn in a strongly acidic solution?
questions.explain: Universal indicator turns red in strongly acidic conditions (low pH).

questions.q: What is one advantage of instrumental methods such as flame emission spectroscopy?
options: They are fast, accurate and use very small samples
questions.explain: Instrumental methods like flame emission spectroscopy are fast, accurate and sensitive, working on tiny samples.

questions.q: Which two substances are both needed for iron to rust?
questions.explain: Rusting of iron requires both water and oxygen to be present.

questions.q: When making copper sulfate crystals from copper oxide and sulfuric acid, how is the excess copper oxide removed?
questions.explain: The unreacted solid copper oxide is filtered off, leaving the copper sulfate solution.

questions.q: What is observed when a small piece of sodium is added to water?
options: It fizzes, moves on the surface and releases hydrogen
It turns the water bright blue
questions.explain: Sodium reacts vigorously with water, fizzing as it produces hydrogen gas and sodium hydroxide.

questions.q: Oxygen gas can be identified because it:
questions.explain: Oxygen relights a glowing splint.

questions.q: To test for halide ions with silver nitrate, why is dilute nitric acid added first?
options: To make the gas test work
To remove carbonate ions that would also give a precipitate
questions.explain: Nitric acid removes carbonate ions so they don't form a precipitate and give a false halide result.

questions.q: Chlorine gas is identified because it:
questions.explain: Chlorine bleaches damp litmus paper, turning it white.

questions.q: When a metal carbonate reacts with an acid, which gas is produced?
questions.explain: Acid + metal carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide.

questions.q: In a titration, which piece of apparatus delivers a precisely measured, fixed volume of one solution?
questions.explain: A pipette is used to measure an accurate fixed volume, while the burette delivers a variable volume.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry (4CH1) specification; Inorganic Chemistry
